## Summary

**Cause:** In `src/click/parser.py`, `_process_opts` split a long option with an attached value using `arg.split("=")[:2]`, which splits on *every* `=` and then keeps only the first two pieces. So `--name=a=b=c` became `("--name", "a")`, silently dropping `b=c`.

**Fix:** Changed it to split only on the first `=`:

```python
long_opt, explicit_value = arg.split("=", 1)
```

This makes everything after the first equals sign the value (`a=b=c`), staying DRY/YAGNI — a one-character fix, no over-engineering, and correctly handles edge cases like empty values (`--name=` → `''`). Verified manually and with the existing parser/options test suite (119 passed).
